audit.recode_to: no reclassification now. On reading Rigsby 1976: keep classification weight (onset-conditioned, left edge) if he states 'first syllable with an onset'; but if Kuku-Thaypan words are overwhelmingly C-initial (full CV1 loss, per Verstraete 2021), the representative pattern string should be the initial-stress series (initial stress) with V-initial second-syllable stress as the minority case, or the record should carry both.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding quotations (Goedemans 1998:135 + App. D VIII pp.248-249; the StressTyp2 entry) are verbatim in copies we hold at the stated locators. (2) The classification rests on a 1998 dissertation's survey appendix and the StressTyp2 entry, both by Goedemans and both carrying the one primary, Rigsby 1976 (9-page descriptive/historical phonology), which we do not hold and could not reach (IA lending-only, Google Books blocked). Glottolog 5.1 lists no grammar or later phonology; no instrumental or JIPA work exists; the language lost its last speaker in 2016. So Rigsby 1976 is the best available source and it is unheld. (3) downloaded now: Blevins 2001 (open, ANU) confirms the historical picture (stress shift to second syllable, invariable C1 loss, citing Rigsby 1976); Verstraete 2021 'Pathways' (open, Lirias) is silent on stress but calls Kuku Thaypan a full-initial-vowel-l

sources.quote: No stress statement for Thaypan; names 'neighbouring languages with full initial vowel loss (for which Lamalama, Kuku Thaypan and Aghu Tharrnggala would be the best candidates; see Rigsby 1976 and Jolly 1989 ...)'. If Kuku Thaypan has lost whole initial syllables (C-initial words the norm), the onset rule yields INITIAL stress in most words and our representative pattern string '01 010 0100...' (built on the assumption that V-initial words are 'the typical shape') may misstate the majority surface pattern; the onset-conditioned classification itself is untouched.

Needed to confirm the exact stress statement, whether V-initial words exist in number (Verstraete 2021 calls Kuku Thaypan a 'full initial vowel loss' language), and hence whether the representative pattern should be initial rather than second stress.
